strengths: Addresses timely and practical problem of democratizing access to expensive reasoning models
Comprehensive evaluation of multiple compression paradigms (quantization, distillation, pruning) on the same models
Diverse selection of reasoning benchmarks spanning different reasoning types (mathematical, logical, temporal, multihop)
Interesting empirical finding that parameter count impacts knowledge memorization more than reasoning capability
Clear presentation with informative tables and reproducibility details
weaknesses: No methodological novelty—purely empirical benchmarking with no new compression techniques or theoretical insights
Severe limitation to single model (DeepSeek-R1 only); claims about 'compressed large reasoning models' lack generalizability
Insufficient evaluation rigor: very small test sets (AIME 30, MuSiQue 100), single pass, no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals
Incomplete baseline comparisons: only one quantization method (Unsloth), limited distillation configurations, SparseGPT mismatch with model sizes
Knowledge vs. reasoning claim lacks rigor—based primarily on one dataset (MuSiQue) under closed-book setting without ablation studies or causal validation
Test-time compute analysis is superficial: treats words as tokens (inaccurate), analyzes only extreme percentiles, causality unclear (shorter outputs vs. easier questions)
Baseline reliability issue: DeepSeek API problems affect R1 performance; 2.51-bit outperforming baseline is unexplained and speculative
Practical metrics missing: no actual inference latency, throughput, or memory consumption measurements despite efficiency being core motivation
For MuSiQue, closed-book setting acknowledged as unrealistic; RAG results missing despite being more suitable approach
No evaluation on other reasoning models (QwQ-32B, etc.) limiting claims about general LRM compression

strengths: Addresses timely and underexplored problem of compression for large reasoning models
Comprehensive benchmarking across multiple compression methods (quantization, distillation, pruning) and reasoning benchmarks (AIME, FOLIO, Temporal, MuSiQue)
Useful practical insight distinguishing impact of parameter count on knowledge memorization vs. reasoning capability
Novel observation on correlation between output length and reasoning performance
Diverse evaluation across benchmarks of varying difficulty levels
weaknesses: Limited novelty: applies existing compression techniques without proposing new methods or theoretical contributions
Unreliable baseline: DeepSeek-R1 API results affected by security mechanisms; claim of quantized model outperforming original undermines confidence
Small sample evaluation: only 100/1000 samples for MuSiQue; no error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing
Multi-platform inference: different tools (llama.cpp, vLLM, API) introduces confounds; impossible to isolate compression effects from platform optimizations
Critical missing evaluation: no inference speedup or latency measurements despite speedup being a primary compression motivation

Test-time compute analysis relies on crude word-counting tokenization instead of standard tokenizers; causality between output length and performance unclear (shorter outputs may be artifacts of failure)
Shallow mechanistic analysis of key findings: knowledge vs. reasoning distinction based on single comparison; collapse point correlation with benchmark difficulty unexplained
Non-standard experimental setup: closed-book MuSiQue evaluation limits generalizability; single-pass evaluation (no multiple runs); no statistical testing despite small sample sizes
Obvious conclusions: some findings unsurprising (smaller distilled models have less knowledge, aggressive pruning causes collapse, fewer parameters = worse performance)
Reproducibility concerns: sampling from MuSiQue makes results non-deterministic; multi-platform setup; no code release mentioned; missing implementation details

strengths: Addresses important gap: Systematic evaluation of compression on LRMs was previously lacking, directly relevant to AI democratization
Comprehensive benchmarking framework: Evaluates three major compression paradigms (quantization, distillation, pruning) across diverse reasoning types and difficulty levels
Actionable insights: Distinguishes compression impact on knowledge vs. reasoning capability, providing practical recommendations (prefer quantization for knowledge-intensive tasks)
Multiple compression levels: Thorough exploration of sparsity levels (0-80%) and bit-widths reveals collapse points and performance trade-offs
Test-time compute analysis: Reveals that shorter outputs generally correlate with better reasoning performance, consistent across models and benchmarks
Well-structured methodology: Clear experimental design with consistent generation parameters and multiple diverse reasoning benchmarks
weaknesses: Missing core efficiency metric: No actual inference speed/latency measurements despite compression being fundamentally about efficiency; this undermines the central motivation
Platform inconsistency: Different inference platforms for different compression methods (llama.cpp vs. vLLM) introduces uncontrolled variables affecting fair comparison

Baseline credibility concerns: DeepSeek API issues (empty responses) requiring iterative prompting potentially bias baseline R1 evaluation; suspicious result that 2.51-bit outperforms original R1 (84.8 vs 83.1)
Methodological mismatch: SparseGPT designed for ~176B models but applied to 70B/32B models without adequate justification
Crude tokenization method: Using word counts as 'tokens' for test-time compute analysis is inaccurate; actual tokenizer outputs would be more rigorous

Limited statistical rigor: No confidence intervals/error bars, single-pass evaluation, small test sets (30 AIME, 100 MuSiQue samples), no significance testing, MuSiQue sampling lacks seed specification
Knowledge vs. reasoning claim under-supported: Only MuSiQue used to evaluate knowledge memorization; additional knowledge-intensive benchmarks needed
Incomplete distillation analysis: Only two student sizes (70B, 32B) evaluated; lacks systematic exploration of smaller models and compression-performance frontier
Limited novelty: Applies existing compression techniques without proposing new methods; primarily descriptive benchmarking rather than mechanistic insights
Reproducibility issues: No code availability mentioned, different inference platforms hinder reproduction, implementation details sparse

strengths: Addresses a timely and well-motivated research gap in understanding compression effects on reasoning models specifically
Comprehensive benchmarking across multiple compression methods (quantization, distillation, pruning) and diverse reasoning datasets with varying difficulty levels

Novel application of mechanistic interpretation techniques (difference of means and attribution patching) to identify fine-grained weight importance per module, more detailed than prior layer-wise analyses
Actionable practical insights: protecting 2% of weights yields 6.57% accuracy improvement, demonstrating clear value of the interpretation analysis
Validation across both Llama and Qwen model families suggests some generalizability of findings
Solid experimental design with multiple runs per model and appropriate baselines
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (heatmaps) that communicate weight importance patterns well
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: mechanistic interpretation techniques (difference of means, attribution patching) are adaptations of recent work by Venhoff et al. and Syed et al.; the core innovation is application rather than methodology

Narrow scope severely limits generalizability: analysis primarily focuses on DeepSeek-R1; other reasoning models (QwQ-32B, etc.) not studied; test sets are very small (AIME 2024 has 30 samples, MuSiQue uses only 100 randomly sampled questions)

Limited theoretical depth: paper characterizes which weights are important but provides minimal mechanistic insight into why (e.g., why is final-layer up_proj critical?); remains largely empirical characterization

Weak validation of mechanistic findings: only selective quantization of a few components tested; simple mixed-precision protection scheme in Table 4 leaves unclear whether insights truly identify critical weights or reflect one possible approach

Insufficient analysis of key findings: pruning collapse not mechanistically explained; 3-4 bit quantization threshold not explained; knowledge vs. reasoning distinction relies solely on MuSiQue which requires both skills

Distillation-compression interaction unclear: distilled models already significantly weaker than full R1 (42.2% vs 73.3% on AIME); difficult to isolate whether findings generalize beyond distilled variants

Reproducibility concerns: code availability statement incomplete ('Our interpretation code is a'); GPT-4o behavior detection procedure not fully specified; mixed inference setups not clearly documented

Missing statistical rigor: no confidence intervals or significance tests; high variability on some metrics (especially MuSiQue) without discussion; impossible to assess statistical significance of differences
Design choices not well justified: setting increases in relative importance to zero is somewhat arbitrary; no ablation on this choice or on selected reasoning behaviors

Incomplete scope analysis: focus on weak 8B and 7B distilled models; analysis depth on larger models (R1-Distill-Llama-70B, Qwen-32B) insufficient; test-time compute analysis underdeveloped despite being interesting

strengths: Addresses an important and timely gap in understanding compression of Large Reasoning Models with comprehensive benchmarking across multiple compression methods
Provides fine-grained mechanistic interpretation by analyzing individual linear modules rather than just layers, improving upon prior work
Practical validation through selective protection experiments demonstrates that protecting ~2% of weights yields 6.57% improvement in 3-bit quantization
Findings generalize across Llama and Qwen model families, showing some robustness
Generally well-organized with clear presentation and helpful visualizations
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: primarily applies existing interpretation techniques (difference of means, attribution patching) to compressed models without advancing these methods
Narrow primary focus on DeepSeek-R1 with limited coverage of other LRM families; cannot apply to closed-source models (o1/o3)
Small dataset sizes (AIME 2024: 30 samples, MuSiQue: only 100 of 1000 samples) and no statistical significance testing weaken conclusions

Flawed interpretation methodology: (1) dropping increases in relative importance lacks justification, (2) relying on GPT-4o to identify reasoning behaviors is noisy and non-reproducible, (3) only 4 behaviors targeted may miss important mechanisms

Finding 1 conflates different compression mechanisms (pruning removes parameters, distillation reduces model size, quantization preserves count); experimental design does not cleanly isolate knowledge vs. reasoning effects
Insufficient mechanistic explanation: paper identifies important weights but provides no causal understanding of why they matter or how to systematically improve compression methods
Pruning shows dramatic collapse but is largely dismissed ('we do not interpret the effect of pruning in later sections') rather than analyzed
Ad-hoc protective mechanism (keeping final-layer modules in 16-bit) does not advance compression methodology; unclear why existing methods over-compress or how to fix them systematically
Reproducibility concerns: promised code is incomplete, GPT-4o prompts not published, reliance on closed-source DeepSeek-R1 API, and unclear MuSiQue sample selection
Missing critical ablations: component-level breakdown of 6.57% improvement, sensitivity analysis of protection strategy, cross-model generalization testing
Test-time compute analysis relegated to appendix despite being critical for LRMs
Unclear differentiation from concurrent work (Liu et al. 2025, Feng et al. 2025, Srivastava et al. 2025) on compressed LRM evaluation

strengths: Addresses timely and important research gap in LRM compression—a significantly underexplored area compared to general LLM compression
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple compression paradigms (7+ quantization methods, distillation variants, pruning) and diverse reasoning benchmarks with varying difficulty
Novel application of mechanistic interpretation techniques at module-level granularity, providing finer-grained weight importance analysis than prior layer-wise approaches
Effective empirical validation through selective quantization experiments (Tables 3-4), demonstrating 6.57% improvement by protecting just 2% of weights
Key findings validated across two model families (Llama and Qwen), suggesting some generalization
Immediately actionable practical insights for guiding future compression method design
Thorough experimental documentation with detailed implementation details and extensive appendices
weaknesses: Limited scope: fine-grained interpretation analysis primarily restricted to DeepSeek-R1 distilled variants; does not evaluate other open-source LRMs (QwQ, etc.) or closed-source models, limiting generalization claims

Interpretability methodology concerns: GPT-4o-based reasoning behavior detection lacks rigor (no inter-annotator agreement, validation metrics, or justification for design choices like 5-token context); circular validation risk in using importance scores for selective protection

Finding 1 (knowledge vs. reasoning distinction) relies primarily on correlational evidence from MuSiQue performance across model sizes; needs stronger causal support through direct probing or targeted ablations

Significant gap in pruning analysis: dismisses pruning after 50% sparsity without interpretation, missing opportunity to understand precise degradation points and providing only anecdotal case studies

MuSiQue evaluation concerns: only 100 sampled questions (high variance), very low absolute performance (17% EM for original R1), no confidence intervals, and minimal gains from selective protection (1.0→1.3 EM)
Insufficient statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; 6.57% improvement demonstrated on only one configuration (Llama-8B + 3-bit AWQ)
No comparison with alternative weight importance metrics (magnitude-based, Fisher information, Hessian-based), making it unclear whether chosen methods are superior
Limited mechanistic insight into why compression creates observed importance shifts; importance patterns are visualized but not deeply analyzed
Incomplete presentation: footnote 1 and similar references incomplete, suggesting rushed submission; dense heatmaps (Figures 2-7) difficult to parse

strengths: Comprehensive empirical benchmarking across multiple compression methods (8+ techniques) and four diverse reasoning datasets, providing thorough evaluation of compression effects on LRMs
Novel application of mechanistic interpretability to understand compression effects at fine-grained (per-module) resolution, advancing beyond previous layer-wise analysis
Well-validated findings with concrete empirical verification: selective quantization experiments validate importance claims, and selective protection improves 3-bit AWQ by 6.57%
Solid experimental design including multiple runs, annotation robustness validation (Table 6), closure-book and RAG settings, and demonstration of generalization to non-R1 models
Addresses timely problem of LRM compression for AI democratization with practical implications for future compression algorithm design
Comprehensive supplementary materials with extensive analysis of generalization, visualization justification, and additional experiments (test-time compute, RAG pipelines, etc.)
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: core techniques (difference of means, attribution patching) are direct applications of existing work; innovation is primarily in domain application rather than new methods

Small annotation dataset (120 instances total) with GPT-4o dependency introduces potential bias and limits coverage of reasoning behavior diversity; behavior definitions appear somewhat arbitrary without sensitivity analysis

Scope and generalization limitations: deep analysis focuses on small distilled models (Llama-8B, Qwen-7B); full R1 (671B) only benchmarked; non-R1 generalization shown on only one additional model (DistilGPT-OSS) in appendix

Incomplete pruning analysis forced to 30% sparsity due to severe degradation, making comparison with 4-bit quantization (4× compression) difficult and limiting understanding of pruning-performance tradeoffs

Proposed solution (selective 16-bit protection of 2% of weights) is overly simple and lacks novel compression methodology; limited guidance on automatic identification of weights to protect or generalization to different architectures

Subjectivity in key design choices: GPT-4o-based behavior definitions from free-form prompts; choice to visualize only importance decreases while justified obscures complete picture; limited mechanistic insight into WHY certain weights matter
Missing statistical rigor: no confidence intervals or significance tests despite LLM output variance; no sensitivity analysis for behavior definitions or context length choices

Incomplete analysis of distillation effects: finding that distilled model weights are 'mainly from distillation' is interesting but lacks depth; mechanisms explaining dramatic weight importance reshaping not explored

strengths: Comprehensive empirical study addressing timely problem of reasoning model compression with multiple methods and diverse datasets
Thorough mechanistic interpretation combining difference of means and attribution patching to achieve fine-grained weight importance analysis
Direct empirical validation of importance claims through selective quantization experiments with measurable performance impacts
Generalization evidence across different distilled model families demonstrated in appendices
Extensive experimental documentation and reproducible implementation details for facilitating future work
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: primarily applies existing interpretation techniques (Arditi et al. 2024, Syed et al. 2023) to compression domain without significant technical innovation
Indirect evidence for Finding 1 (weight count vs reasoning): comparing models of different sizes conflates multiple factors, and knowledge-reasoning distinction is unclear in practice

Inconsistent support for Finding 2: Table 3 shows variable importance of components across runs/settings, contradicting claim of consistent final-layer up_proj criticality; finding specific to distilled models with unclear generalization
Finding 3 solution is ad-hoc: mixed-precision protection conflicts with inference optimization requirements and relies on manually selecting 2% of weights without principled methodology

Confounded experimental design: different quantization methods use different calibration data, inference runs on different platforms, and annotation uses only 120 instances with single LLM-based labeler
Pruning severely underexplored: model collapse forced analysis at 30-50% sparsity preventing fair comparison with quantization methods, weakening claims about knowledge sensitivity
Insufficient statistical rigor: lacks confidence intervals, significance testing, and variance reporting for major claims; variability in single-pass evaluations not quantified
Limited generalization scope: findings primarily tested on 8B/7B distilled R1 models; scalability to larger models, non-distilled variants, and different architectures largely unexplored
Small benchmark scale: AIME has only 30 examples; MuSiQue randomly sampled without justification; low absolute scores on knowledge tasks limit confidence in conclusions
Findings are incremental: core insights (preserve important weights, final layers matter) largely confirm intuitions rather than revealing surprising patterns or mechanisms

strengths: Addresses important and timely problem of compressing large reasoning models with comprehensive benchmarking across three compression paradigms and multiple methods
Novel mechanistic interpretation approach using fine-grained analysis of every linear module to identify critical weights for specific reasoning behaviors
Strong empirical validation with practical improvements (6.57% accuracy gain by protecting 2% of weights, up to 23.17% over baselines) through targeted experiments
Excellent presentation with comprehensive appendices (27 pages) including robustness checks, generalization studies, and clear implementation details
Results generalize beyond primary models with evidence from non-R1 LRM families, addressing a key concern
Identifies actionable bottlenecks in current quantization methods that can guide future algorithm design
weaknesses: Limited model diversity - primarily DeepSeek-R1 variants with only one additional non-R1 model tested; cannot evaluate closed-source LRMs
Small annotation dataset (120 instances) for extracting reasoning behaviors with potential bias toward specific behavior types in this sample
Limited mechanistic insight into why findings hold - identifies what is important but provides insufficient explanation of why final-layer up_projection is critical for reasoning
Inconsistency in findings (Table 3 anomaly where 1_up shows lowest AIME 2024 accuracy despite lower importance ranking) raises questions about metric reliability
Practical limitations of proposed solution - mixed-precision approach may not be hardware-efficient; no inference speedup analysis
Knowledge vs reasoning claim based on comparing different architectures (70B Llama vs 32B Qwen) with limited controlled evidence
Very low performance on MuSiQue (R1 baseline ~27% F1) limits conclusions about knowledge retention effects
Interpretation methodology questions: normalization choice in difference of means lacks justification, connection between cross-entropy loss and reasoning quality unclear
